answer: Membership rests on a relic, not on a wallet address. Each relic carries a single custody ledger: a transfer needs the outgoing holder's signature and the epoch beacon stamp, and any second claim on the same relic is void, so two clones presenting one artifact collide in public. Genuine relics hold long co-signed histories and none can be minted, so a k-seat farm needs k distinct artifacts bought from k distinct holders, and demand against fixed supply makes each further purchase dearer. A whisper of a forged custody link is cheap for auditors to check and fatal to the claim.
